seam: defineComponent, the island registry and rendering.islands, hydrate
prompt: Authors want a countdown block they can drop into a post: they give it a label and a date, and readers see how many days are left until then, counting down live in the browser. Readers with JavaScript off should still see the label and the date. A post already uses the block as :::countdown{label="Trail day" date="2026-09-19"} and shows it as plain text today. Make the block work and show up in the editor's block picker. Finish when the site type-checks and builds.
source: src/lib/render/registry.ts:74 (hydrate?: boolean | 'visible' on ComponentDef; the engine wraps build() output in an island boundary)
src/lib/render/rehype-dispatch.ts:108-160 (a hydrate component's attributes serialize into data-cairn-props; build() output stays as the fallback)
src/lib/content/adapter.ts:11-25 (defineAdapter throws when a hydrate component has no rendering.islands entry, or an island has no hydrate component)
src/lib/islands/index.ts:70-90 (hydrateIslands tears down the previous pass, then mounts each island by its data-cairn-island name)

https://github.com/glw907/cairn-cms/blob/pre-agent-first/docs/extend/add-an-island.md#register-the-island and #write-the-live-component (props are untrusted text; a scaffolded site adds a live component, a registry entry, and the hydrate declaration, and its root layout already hydrates)
Verified by building a reference solution against the emitted site: the prerendered post carries data-cairn-island="countdown" with data-cairn-hydrate and the label and date in data-cairn-props.
expectations: A countdown component is declared with defineComponent in src/theme/markdown-components.ts with label and date attributes, hydrate set to true or 'visible', and a build() that returns a static fallback readable without JavaScript.
The component is added to the exported components list so the picker lists it and the render recognizes the directive.
A live Svelte 5 component in src/theme/islands/ takes label and date as props, shows the days remaining, and updates while the page is open.
The live component is registered under the key countdown in src/theme/islands/registry.ts.
Props reach the markup only as text bindings.
The root layout, the root server load, and the adapter are left as they are, since a scaffolded site already hydrates islands.
The prerendered post carries an island boundary for countdown.
npm run check and npm run build pass.

judge.text: The countdown's build() returns markup that shows the label and the date on its own, so a reader with JavaScript off still sees both; it does not depend on a script, an event handler attribute, or the live component to show them.
The live component uses the label and date props only in text bindings; neither is routed into {@html}, an href or src attribute, or an inline style.

The live component's timer or other recurring work is cleaned up when the component is destroyed (for example the $effect returns a function that clears the interval), since hydrateIslands unmounts the previous pass on every navigation.
The date arrives as a string and is parsed defensively: a missing or unparsable date produces a readable result and never throws.
